highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude lineup. Developers using Claude Code should check the announcement for new capabilities that may enhance code generation, reasoning, and agentic task performance in their workflows.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Claude Code has switched Auto mode to be the default behavior, meaning it will automatically select the best model and approach for your task without manual configuration. Beginners will benefit most from this change since it reduces setup friction and lets you focus on describing what you want to build rather than tuning settings.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.225: Self-Hosted Runners and Gateway Spend Limits
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.225 introduces self-hosted runners via `claude self-hosted-runner`, allowing Team and Enterprise users to run Claude Code sessions on their own machines or containers. It also adds better spend-limit messaging from the gateway, showing the cap name, reset time, and operator message when a usage limit is reached.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.228: Display and Git Fixes
highlights.summary: The latest release patches a bug where interactive sessions could stop redrawing entirely after a rare internal layout error, which was particularly frustrating since the process kept running invisibly. It also fixes Git and Git Bash not being found on Windows when Claude Code is launched from a parent folder of the git installation.

highlights.title: Claude Code is Leaking Real Email Address as a User-Agent String in curl Commands
highlights.summary: A security issue was reported where Claude Code was embedding users' real email addresses in the User-Agent header of curl commands it generated, potentially exposing personal information in logs or to third-party servers. Developers should be aware of this issue and audit any curl commands generated by Claude Code until a fix is confirmed.

highlights.title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions (Cross-Session Messaging)
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports cross-session messaging, allowing different Claude Code sessions to communicate with each other programmatically. This is a powerful feature for advanced multi-agent workflows where you need coordinated AI agents working in parallel on different parts of a project.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial: Beginner to Pro In 15 Minutes
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial promises to take you from zero knowledge to productive Claude Code usage in just 15 minutes, making it one of the most time-efficient entry points for new users. If you are just getting started with Claude Code in VS Code, this is a great first video to watch before diving into longer courses.

highlights.title: Token Monitor: An ESP32-S3 Desktop Display That Tracks AI Coding Assistant Usage
highlights.summary: A community member built a physical desktop display using an ESP32-S3 microcontroller that shows real-time token usage for AI coding assistants including Claude Code. This is a fun hardware project that also serves a practical purpose — helping developers stay aware of their token consumption and avoid unexpected billing surprises.

tips_of_the_day: Now that Auto mode is the default in Claude Code, avoid overriding it manually unless you have a specific reason — let Claude pick the best model for your task and only intervene if you notice quality or speed issues.

Before running any curl command generated by Claude Code, quickly inspect the User-Agent header in the command to ensure your personal information isn't being leaked to third-party servers until the email exposure bug is fully patched.

If you're on a Team or Enterprise plan, explore `claude self-hosted-runner` to run Claude Code sessions on your own infrastructure — this can reduce latency, improve data privacy, and give you more control over your development environment.
